question.problem: Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =6.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =6.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-5{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-5{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}={x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
